artworks.title: Boreas Abducting Oreithyia
artworks.description: Solimena paints the North Wind carrying Oreithyia — the abduction that begets Chione, Cleopatra, Zetes and Calais. Chione is the snow-daughter of that Thracian marriage, mother of Eumolpus by Poseidon.

artworks.title: Boreas Abducting Oreithyia (detail)
artworks.description: Detail of Solimena's canvas: Oreithyia in Boreas' grip — the parents of Chione of Thrace, not Chione daughter of Daedalion whom Artemis slew.

artworks.title: Boreas Abducting Oreithyia (Vienna)
artworks.description: Kunsthistorisches Museum version of the same rape: the founding scene of Chione's Boread house.

artworks.title: Boreas and Oreithyia
artworks.description: Attic pointed amphora: Boreas seizes Oreithyia — the classical image of the parents who will raise Chione beside the winged Argonauts Zetes and Calais.

popCulture.title: Chione (daughter of Boreas)
popCulture.description: Daughter of Boreas and Oreithyia; by Poseidon mother of Eumolpus — not Chione daughter of Daedalion, mother of Autolycus.

popCulture.title: Eumolpus
popCulture.description: Chione's son by Poseidon — the Eleusinian founder whose lineage keeps her name in Attic cult myth.
